title: Thevenin equivalent of a 12 V divider
caption: A 12 V source with 4 Ω and 6 Ω in a divider, output across the 6 Ω: open-circuit voltage V_th = 12 × 6/10 = 7.2 V, and R_th = 4 ∥ 6 = 2.4 Ω (source shorted). Any load then sees V = V_th − I R_th: a straight line from 7.2 V at no load to the short-circuit (Norton) current I_N = V_th/R_th = 3 A at V = 0.
alt: Graph of output voltage against load current: a straight line from 7.2 V at zero current to 3 A at zero volts, gradient −2.4 ohms.
description: The horizontal axis is the current drawn by the load in amperes; the vertical axis is the output voltage in volts.
With no load (I = 0) the output is the open-circuit voltage V_th = 7.2 V.
The line falls by R_th = 2.4 V per ampere: it is the Thevenin source's V = V_th − I R_th.
Shorting the output gives the Norton current 3 A.
